findings.title: Unsubscribe is a GET that mutates notification level
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed as GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Mail clients, link scanners, and antivirus gateways prefetch URLs in notification emails, so merely receiving or opening the message can change the recipient's topic notification level. The action is also not idempotent: a watching or tracking user is first dropped to regular, and a refresh or second prefetch then mutes them. State changes from an email link need a POST (or a single-use token) and must not keep downgrading on repeat requests.

findings.title: Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
findings.body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(...) and then calls tu.notification_level with no nil check. Users can be emailed about a topic without an existing topic_users row (or the row can be absent for other reasons). Clicking the new email link then raises NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing, so the feature 500s for exactly the people the link is meant to serve. Use TopicUser.change, which creates the row when missing.

findings.title: Direct save leaves unsubscribe reversible by auto-track
findings.body: The new action assigns notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. change sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and notifications_changed_at, and publishes the level change. A raw save leaves notifications_reason_id nil. update_last_read then auto-promotes the user back to tracking whenever total time viewed exceeds the auto-track threshold, silently undoing the unsubscribe on the next visit or timing update. The open topic UI also never receives the MessageBus notification_level_change.

findings.title: Preloaded topic JSON still has the old notification level
findings.body: TopicView is built before the TopicUser row is updated, and perform_show_response serializes that same @topic_view into the preloaded topic payload. The notifications control on the page therefore still shows watching/tracking/regular after the server has already changed the level. The user is told notifications have stopped while the button shows the previous state, and using that button can write the stale level back.

findings.title: Watching users are not actually unsubscribed
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets regular instead of muted. Watching is the level that emails every reply, and the new server string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic." After one click a watcher is still at regular, so mentions and replies-to-you still notify, and the client copy ("You will stop receiving notifications") is shown unconditionally. Only a second request mutes them, which is not what the email promises.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template is not registered for its route
findings.body: The Ember route is declared as topicUnsubscribe (templates/topic-unsubscribe, controller topic-unsubscribe). This file lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which Ember resolves only for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. After the full-page load boots the app, the topicUnsubscribe route has no template, so the confirmation text and topic-notifications-button never render. Move the template to topic-unsubscribe.hbs (or nest the route under topic and point it at this template).

findings.title: No coverage for the unsubscribe action
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder and still does not assert that the topic link is rendered. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted, repeat requests, slug redirect, or that the preloaded payload matches the saved level. Those paths are easy to regress and currently untested.
